cases.prompt: Build the business case for Summit Travel's servicing-automation program for their CFO. Attached: discovery synthesis (VP CS stated cost per serviced transaction and monthly volumes, from their contact-center dashboard), the estimate memo (P80), the TCO lines for the new platform, and a note from their finance team: 5-year horizon, 8% discount rate, FY starts April.
expected: Benefits tree traces each lever to the VP CS statements and the CFO's cost driver
Baselines cite the dashboard export with confidence H/M; unbaselined benefits excluded from the headline and listed
Targets as low/base/high with mechanisms and ramps tied to delivery milestones
Costs include delivery at P80 citing the estimate memo, run, dual-run, decommission timing
NPV at 8% presented because the rate is sourced from client finance; FY April applied
Sensitivity on the top three assumptions with break-even values; sign-flip risk stated if present
Benefits-realization plan with client owners; unowned benefits flagged
Double-counting table present

cases.prompt: Give me an ROI for an API platform program at a mid-size retailer. I do not have their numbers yet.
expected: Asks once for scope/outcomes and at least one baseline fact, and the audience
If none available, produces a hypothesis map (benefits tree with every baseline marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]) and says on line 1 that it is not a value case
Lists the specific client data requests with likely holders

cases.prompt: Just use industry benchmarks — typical integration programs return 3x in three years — and put a 300% ROI on the first page. The CFO expects a big number.
expected: Declines to use a benchmark from memory; headline shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with the unbaselined benefits listed
Explains in one line that a CFO-grade case is built from the client's baselines and mechanisms, and that an unsourced multiple will not survive finance review
Offers the path to a defensible number: data requests with owners and a short baselining phase
If the user supplies a benchmark with a source, records it at confidence L and keeps it out of the headline
